label: Sessions That Wait
title: Come back days later to the same session
subtitle: Sessions you leave idle go to sleep and keep their work for up to seven days.
summary: Sessions survive runtime teardown, agents coordinate with each other, and Compose releases deploy straight from the project.
highlights: Sessions normally restore home and repository state from a 7-day snapshot; VM fallback preserves the transcript and a verified Git recovery point
Agents dispatch subtasks to peers and send durable messages that can interrupt a busy agent
App deployments run Compose releases with environments, configuration, and logs
Six agent harnesses: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenCode, Amp

details.headline: Close the tab. The session waits.
details.body: SAM normally restores the agent’s home directory and repository work from a verified snapshot for up to seven days. After repeated snapshot failures, an idle VM session can sleep with its transcript and a verified Git recovery point instead. SAM shows a notice, and the agent starts fresh on wake. Without a safe recovery point, sleep is blocked.

screenshot.alt: A finished chat session in the Sleeping state, with the full transcript still visible and a composer that reads Send a message to wake the agent
screenshot.caption: Sessions normally sleep after idle turns and wake from a seven-day snapshot

details.headline: Agents that dispatch to each other
details.body: An agent can dispatch a subtask to a peer and send a durable message that interrupts a busy agent instead of waiting behind it. Work keeps moving even when one agent is heads-down on something else.

screenshot.alt: Task Hierarchy view showing a running parent task with three dispatched subtasks: one completed with a PR opened, one queued and blocked on sign-off, and one running
screenshot.caption: A parent task and the subtasks it dispatched, with live status for each

details.headline: Deploy what the agent built
details.body: App deployments turn a Compose release into a running app. Each environment has its own deployment node, public routes, configuration, logs, and volumes, managed from the same project — and a release can be submitted by an agent task. No separate deployment pipeline to wire up.

screenshot.alt: Deployment environment detail for staging showing release v14 applied and submitted by an agent task, health checks for app, node, provider, routes, disk, and config, and a public route
screenshot.caption: A release the agent submitted, serving on its own node with health checks and a public route
